text: Buying online? You check reviews first, right? You want five-star ratings for quality, to make the best choice and avoid duds.
Scrolling, something feels off. Glowing praise, generic language. Identical reviews for unknown products. This feels like artificial enthusiasm.
You try to spot fakes: vague phrases, bad grammar, no details. Bots or eager fans? No, the pattern is too widespread and organized.
The real system: incentives. High ratings mean sales. Businesses pay for positive reviews—with products, discounts, or cash. Trust becomes a traded commodity.
The cost? Wasted time, eroded trust. That five-star rating, once reliable, now feels like a paid ad. The system pollutes information, making decisions harder.
Tomorrow, you'll read reviews. But you'll see the tells: vague praise, rating spikes. You're a detective now, wise to these hidden incentives.
